Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f725945..54bb57f0a 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File Modified:** `core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java`

**Modification:** Changed the upper bound of a Unicode range check used to determine RTL (Right-To-Left) characters. The range `0xFE70 to 0xFEFF` was narrowed to `0xFE70 to 0xFEFE`, excluding the character `0xFEFF` from being classified as RTL.

**Relationship/Reasoning:** This is a single-file, single-line fix. The character `0xFEFF` is a special Unicode marker (Zero Width No-Break Space / Byte Order Mark), not an actual RTL script character, but it fell within the Arabic Presentation Forms-B range (`0xFE70–0xFEFF`) used by the `isRTLCharacter` (or similarly named) method to detect RTL text. By excluding `0xFEFF` from this range, the patch ensures this marker is no longer incorrectly treated as an RTL character, fixing text direction/layout issues wherever this method is used to determine bidirectional text handling.

Here is the commit message:
RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem
in which the 0xFEFF mark was wrongly handled as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

Here is the root cause:
The RTL-detection logic in TextUtils incorrectly included the character 0xFEFF within the Unicode range check `0xFE70–0xFEFF` (Arabic Presentation Forms-B block) used to identify RTL characters. However, 0xFEFF is not an actual RTL script character—it is the Zero Width No-Break Space, commonly used as a Byte Order Mark (BOM) or invisible formatting character. Because it fell within the inclusive range boundary, any text containing this special marker was wrongly classified as containing RTL content, causing incorrect bidirectional text handling/layout decisions.

Here is the patch:
 
     public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
         //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
         return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)`
Reason:
This range check was intended to capture the Arabic Presentation Forms-B Unicode block (0xFE70–0xFEFE), but the upper bound was mistakenly set to 0xFEFF instead of 0xFEFE. Since 0xFEFF is the Zero Width No-Break Space/Byte Order Mark and not an actual RTL character, including it in this range caused `isRTLCharacter` to incorrectly return true whenever this special marker was present, leading to text being wrongly classified as RTL content.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)`
Reason:
By changing the upper bound from 0xFEFF to 0xFEFE, the range now correctly matches only the actual Arabic Presentation Forms-B characters and excludes 0xFEFF. This ensures that the Zero Width No-Break Space/BOM marker is no longer misidentified as an RTL character, fixing the incorrect bidirectional text handling caused by this special character.
